ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

schatzker — pattern 1

A young adult sustains a knee injury from a lateral force with axial loading. CT shows a vertical split through the lateral tibial plateau, but the joint surface is not depressed. The medial plateau and metaphyseal-diaphyseal continuity remain intact. Which Schatzker type best matches the CT description?

  1. Type III
  2. Type IV
  3. Type V
  4. Type I
  5. Type II
Answer and explanation

Type I

Type I: A pure split of the lateral tibial plateau without articular depression.

Option explanations

Type I: Type I: A pure split of the lateral tibial plateau without articular depression.

Type II: Type II describes a lateral plateau split combined with articular depression. The case instead matches Type I.

Type III: Type III describes a pure depression of the lateral plateau without a lateral cortical split. The case instead matches Type I.

Type IV: Type IV describes a fracture involving the medial tibial plateau. The case instead matches Type I.

Type V: Type V describes a bicondylar tibial plateau fracture without complete metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation. The case instead matches Type I.
